title: LAMBDAZERO generates an experimentally active soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor scaffold
summary: The LAMBDAZERO generative active-learning workflow searched for synthesizable soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) inhibitors and produced a quinazoline scaffold absent from the authors' comparison set of known sEH inhibitors. A synthesized analog, UM0152893, inhibited sEH in vitro with sub-micromolar potency.
ai_technology: LAMBDAZERO generative active learning with deep reinforcement learning and docking
organization: Mila – Quebec AI Institute; Université de Montréal; University of Toronto; collaborators

evidence.tested: The LAMBDAZERO generative active-learning workflow searched for synthesizable soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) inhibitors and produced a quinazoline scaffold absent from the authors' comparison set of known sEH inhibitors.
evidence.unknown: This is a workshop paper/preprint rather than a clinical study. The reported lead is a biochemical inhibitor of purified sEH; no cellular, animal, safety or therapeutic outcome is established. The authors report 24/35 synthesized analogs active in vitro with potency spanning roughly 90 μM to 0.4 μM; one best lead is sub-micromolar.
evidence.ai_role: The generative model searched molecular space using docking, synthesizability and drug-likeness constraints and proposed the scaffold; researchers synthesized analogs and measured enzyme inhibition in biochemical assays.
